mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates and stimulates equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions and economic weakness, triggering short-term equity sell-offs as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate increases (FEDFUNDS) and low unemployment (UNRATE) signal over-tightening monetary policy without sufficient labor market support, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25pp in 3 months AND UNRATE < 4.0%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 3 months and UNRATE < 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) during late-cycle expansions signals robust corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods classified as late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals expanding economic activity and rising corporate hiring, boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1.0% over three months signals manufacturing contraction and economic slowdown, triggering equity market corrections as investors price in reduced corporate output, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls > 1.0% in 3 months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) combined with persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary policy failure to control inflation, leading to heightened volatility and negative equity returns as aggressive rate hikes are anticipated.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% month-over-month and FEDFUNDS < 2.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) during housing market recoveries signals increased consumer confidence and construction activity, supporting broader economic growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST growth exceeds 0.3% month-over-month, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
